addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	import AppKit
2	import SwiftUI
3	
4	/// A drag from the workroom tab bar into the split content (content-local point + the dragged tab's id).
5	struct WorkroomPaneDrag: Equatable {
6	  let sid: SidebarID
7	  var location: CGPoint
8	}
9	
10	/// Workroom-into-workroom split renderer (issue #23 follow-up): renders `PaneLayout<SidebarID>` as
11	/// nested, resizable panes — each a full `TargetTerminalDetail`. Deliberately SEPARATE from the
12	/// terminal renderer `PaneTreeView` (whose re-parenting/blank-pane history makes surgery risky); it
13	/// reuses only the pure `PaneTreeLayout` geometry + the generic `PaneLayout` model and duplicates a
14	/// little view chrome (divider, focus border, drop band).
15	///
16	/// Like `PaneTreeView`, panes are laid out in ONE flat `ZStack`, positioned by absolute frames and
17	/// keyed by `SidebarID`, so a surviving pane keeps the exact same host across a layout change (only its
18	/// frame moves) — its terminal is never re-parented. `RootView` ALWAYS renders through this view when
19	/// the tab bar is on (a no-split case is just `.leaf(selected)`), so single↔split is a leaf-set change,
20	/// not a structural swap — the same lesson that made `WorkroomTerminalsView` always render through
21	/// `PaneTreeView`.
22	struct WorkroomSplitView: View {
23	  /// The app store, threaded to each leaf as a plain (non-observed) reference so the workroom
24	  /// context menu (issue #112) can read/mutate it WITHOUT subscribing this terminal-hosting view
25	  /// tree to the whole churny store. NOT `@EnvironmentObject`/`@ObservedObject` on purpose.
26	  let store: AppStore
27	  let layout: PaneLayout<SidebarID>
28	  /// Resolve a leaf to its live target (drops a since-deleted workroom). Owned by the store.
29	  let resolve: (SidebarID) -> TerminalTarget?
30	  let focusedID: SidebarID?
31	  /// The live drag of a workroom into the content — from the tab bar OR a split member's group title
32	  /// bar (issue #110). Drives the drop-edge highlight; a member's title bar writes it while dragging.
33	  @Binding var externalDrag: WorkroomPaneDrag?
34	  /// Content-local point for a global drag location (nil when over the title-bar strip). Owned by
35	  /// `RootView`; shared with the tab bar so a title-bar drag drops onto the same panes a chip would.
36	  let localize: (CGPoint) -> CGPoint?
37	  /// Where a drag at a global location lands (member pane + edge), or nil if not over a pane.
38	  let dropTarget: (CGPoint) -> (sid: SidebarID, edge: PaneEdge)?
39	  let onFocus: (SidebarID) -> Void
40	  let onSetRatio: (CGFloat, UUID) -> Void
41	  let onClose: (SidebarID) -> Void
42	  /// Move a member to land beside another at an edge (drag a group by its title bar). Wired to
43	  /// `store.insertWorkroomSplit`, the same transform the tab-bar chip drop uses.
44	  let onMove: (SidebarID, SidebarID, PaneEdge) -> Void
45	
46	  private static let space = "workroomSplitContent"
47	  /// The gutter holding the pane cards off the left/right sidebars (issue #110). Unconditional since
48	  /// issue #139 — a solo workroom is a card too. **Shared** because `RootView`'s chip-drop hit-testing
49	  /// plans against the *unpadded* detail rect and must subtract this, or every drop lands 6pt off the
50	  /// pane the renderer actually drew (a drop inside the gutter would split with no preview shown).
51	  static let outerGutter: CGFloat = 6
52	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
53	
54	  /// The divider ratio being dragged right now — held here rather than written to the store on every
55	  /// mouse-moved tick. `store.setWorkroomSplitRatio` publishes `workroomSplits`, which invalidates
56	  /// `RootView` and rebuilds every pane (and every pane title bar) at cursor rate; local state keeps
57	  /// the churn inside this view and commits once on mouse-up. Same pattern as `SidebarColumn`'s
58	  /// resize handle.
59	  @State private var liveRatio: (split: UUID, ratio: CGFloat)?
60	
61	  var body: some View {
62	    let leaves = layout.tabIDs
63	    let multi = leaves.count >= 2
64	    let shown = displayedLayout
65	    GeometryReader { geo in
66	      let plan = PaneTreeLayout.plan(shown, in: CGRect(origin: .zero, size: geo.size))
67	      ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {
68	        ForEach(leaves, id: \.self) { sid in
69	          if let target = resolve(sid), let rect = plan.panes[sid] {
70	            WorkroomPaneLeaf(
71	              store: store, sid: sid, target: target, focused: sid == focusedID, multi: multi,
72	              externalDrag: $externalDrag, localize: localize, dropTarget: dropTarget,
73	              onClose: { onClose(sid) }, onMove: onMove
74	            )
75	            .frame(width: rect.width, height: rect.height)
76	            .position(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY)
77	            .id(sid)
78	            // A tap on the pane *chrome* focuses it. Clicking *into* the terminal is handled by the
79	            // first-responder → selection callback (the libghostty NSView eats SwiftUI taps).
80	            .onTapGesture { onFocus(sid) }
81	          }
82	        }
83	        ForEach(plan.dividers) { d in
84	          WorkroomSplitDivider(
85	            orientation: d.orientation, ratio: d.ratio, total: d.total,
86	            onLive: { liveRatio = (d.id, $0) },
87	            onCommit: {
88	              liveRatio = nil
89	              onSetRatio($0, d.id)
90	            }
91	          )
92	          .frame(width: d.hitRect.width, height: d.hitRect.height)
93	          .position(x: d.rect.midX, y: d.rect.midY)
94	        }
95	        dropHighlight(plan: plan)
96	      }
97	      .coordinateSpace(.named(Self.space))
98	    }
99	    // Applied outside the GeometryReader so the panes reflow within the inset.
100	    .padding(.horizontal, Self.outerGutter)

aiTitle: Review card highlight logic for security

content.text:
This change is purely a UI/visual refactor in a SwiftUI view: it renames a parameter (`focused` → `highlighted`) across three helper view/functions and introduces a pure predicate `isHighlighted(focused:multi:) = focused && multi` so a solo pane no longer wears the accent treatment.

There is no security surface touched by the diff:
- No shell/exec, SQL, filesystem, or outbound network sinks.
- No parsing, validation, or authorization logic.
- No logging/telemetry of any user- or model-supplied values.
- No IPC or cross-process boundary.
- No changes to permissions, allowlists, or identity registries.
- The only new logic is a boolean AND used to pick a `Color` for a `RoundedRectangle` stroke/fill/shadow.
- Test changes mirror the rename and add coverage for the new predicate.

Nothing to flag.
